title: Sample 13-4: Poem with Discernible Lines of Poetry

illustrates.quote: Use normal poetry format when the indentions of irregular lines of poetry form a discernible pattern. (See Sample 13-4: Poem with Discernible Lines of Poetry on page 13-17.)

blocks.features: e.e. cummings's "Buffalo Bill's", with irregular but discernible stepped indentions, several run-together compound words, and the author's name given in lower case at the end.

lines.text: and what i want to know is
how do you like your blueeyed boy

blocks.features: Author attribution, lower case, at the end.

print.notes: Picture on PDF p.371; the stepped indentions (deepest at 'stallion' and 'Jesus') form a visually discernible staircase pattern, matching this sample's title.
print.printFeatures: Bold blue title; plain body-text poem; the run-together words 'onetwothreefourfive' and 'pigeonsjustlikethat' are printed with no internal spaces.

lines: h[ d y l yr blueey$ boy
braille.notes: Verbatim from .txt lines 10751-10766, after stripping a 5-char line-number field (2-digit max line number 16, +3=5) and converting U+2800. Title (line 1) is centred. Poem lines follow print's own staggered indentions directly in braille cells: cell 1 (0 indent) for 'Buffalo Bill's'/'defunct'/'and break...'/'he was...'/'how do you...'/'Mister Death'; cell 3 (2-cell indent) for 'who used to'/'ride a...'/'and what i want...'; cell 7 (6-cell indent) for 'stallion'; cell 11 (10-cell indent) for 'Jesus' (matching, i.e. directly reproducing, the print's own discernible staircase pattern, per rule 13.6.1, rather than normalising to a fixed 1-3/1-5 scheme). Attribution 'e.e. cummings' is indented 4 cells (cell 5).

resolution: Run A and run B independently transcribed this item's braille.lines identically, character-for-character; independently re-verified against the cited source .txt lines (U+2800 blank cells / ASCII-space converted, reference-line-number or box-margin field measured and stripped per this section's own convention) as part of this reconciliation. print.blocks content agreed in substance between both runs (only prose-wording differences in `features`/`notes`, not resolved as errors); run A's wording is kept. See compare-gold-13/differences.md for the file-by-file account. CORRECTION during buildModel13 integration: print.blocks poem line 'and what i want to know is' had indent:1 (run A) vs indent:2 (run B) -- an A/B disagreement not caught by the braille.lines-only diff (both runs' braille.lines for this line are identical, '    & :at i want to "k is', 4 leading cells). Resolved in favour of run B (2): nestedMargins's first=level*2 gives 4 only for level 2, not level 1 (which would give 2). CORRECTION during buildModel13 integration: the poem was modelled as a single stanza (both runs), but the gold braille has a blank line between 'Jesus' and 'he was a handsome man' (.txt line 10761, a genuine numbered blank braille row) -- a real stanza break in e.e. cummings's own poem, missed by both runs' print.blocks. Split into two stanzas at this point so buildModel13 inserts the stanza-break indicator (parsePoem's own {type:'indicator', kind:'line'} between <linegroup> siblings) that produces the blank line. CORRECTION during buildModel13 integration: 'e.e. cummings' (the poet's own signature after the poem) was modelled as an ordinary 'paragraph' (both runs), which Emboss's shared default paragraph margin renders 2 cells in -- the gold braille has it 4 cells in ('    e4e4 cumm+s'), exactly BANA §9.4's attribution margin (cell 5, blocked). Changed to 'attribution'.
